title_en: Jilin Metallurgical Equipment Factory v. Yantai Metallurgical Research Institute — dispute over a processing contract

full_text_en:
Jilin Metallurgical Equipment Plant v.  
Yantai Metallurgical Research Institute — dispute over processing and fabrication contract  

[Ruling Summary]  

1. Where an agreement is signed after negotiation between the parties, and one party modifies certain terms when affixing its seal while the other party raises no written objection, it shall be deemed that the modified agreement has been accepted.  

2. Where a processing and fabrication contract provides that the contractor shall deliver the manufactured and installed equipment to the ordering party only after debugging and acceptance, if the contractor has conducted multiple debugging sessions but the parties have not gone through the equipment acceptance procedures and there is no other evidence proving that the equipment has been debugged and accepted, the fact that the ordering party has made partial payments for the equipment cannot alone establish that the ordered equipment has been debugged and accepted.  

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People’s Court  

(2002) Min Er Ti Zi No. 16  

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute.  
Domicile: No. 1, Mudanjiang Road, Economic and Technological Development Zone, Yantai City, Shandong Province.  
Legal Representative: Hao Guangzheng, Director of the Institute.  
Agent ad litem: Zhai Ying, Employee of the Institute.  
Agent ad litem: Zhao Qimin, Office Director of the Institute.  

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant.  
Domicile: No. 25-2, Xinshan Road, Longtan District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.  
Legal Representative: Ji Peng, Plant Manager.  
Agent ad litem: Liu Pinxiang, Attorney at Beijing Century Law Firm.  
Agent ad litem: Wang Zhongguo, Legal Advisor of Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant.  

With respect to the dispute over a processing and fabrication contract between Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Yantai Metallurgical Institute) and Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant (hereinafter referred to as Jilin Equipment Plant), the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court rendered Civil Judgment (1998) Ji Jing Zai Zi No. 26 on June 25, 1998, which has already taken legal effect. Yantai Metallurgical Institute, dissatisfied with that judgment, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by Civil Ruling (2002) Min Er Jian Zi No. 84 on March 19, 2002, decided to bring the case up for retrial and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear the case. The trial has now been concluded.  

Upon retrial, this Court finds the following facts:  

On November 4, 1987, and February 1, 1988, Yantai Metallurgical Institute and Jilin Equipment Plant successively entered into contracts for the manufacture of a pre-oxidation furnace and an asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace. The pre-oxidation furnace manufacturing contract provided that Yantai Metallurgical Institute would provide three sets of manufacturing drawings, be responsible for the supporting public facilities such as power supply, water supply, and oxygen supply in the production workshop, provide the equipment debugging outline, and participate in partial debugging. Jilin Equipment Plant was responsible for the processing and manufacture of the pre-oxidation furnace, resolving technical issues arising during its processing and manufacture, and participating in the debugging of the pre-oxidation furnace. The complete set of pre-oxidation furnace was to be completed by the end of September 1988. The total manufacturing fee was RMB 350,000. Within two weeks after the contract took effect, Yantai Metallurgical Institute was to pay Jilin Equipment Plant RMB 110,000; after the equipment arrived, it was to pay 50% of the total manufacturing fee; and the remaining manufacturing fee was to be paid in one lump sum after the equipment was installed, debugged, and accepted at Yantai Metallurgical Institute. The asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace manufacturing contract provided that Yantai Metallurgical Institute would provide three sets of manufacturing drawings, be responsible for the supporting public facilities such as power supply, water supply, and nitrogen supply in the production workshop, provide the equipment debugging outline, and participate in partial debugging. Jilin Equipment Plant was responsible for the processing and manufacture of the asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace, resolving technical issues arising during its processing and manufacture, and the on-site installation and debugging of the complete set of equipment. The complete set of carbonization furnace equipment was to be dispatched from Jilin by the end of November 1988. The total manufacturing fee was RMB 420,000. The settlement method was as follows: within two weeks after the contract took effect, Yantai Metallurgical Institute was to pay Jilin Equipment Plant RMB 126,000; after the equipment arrived, it was to pay 50% of the total manufacturing fee; and the remaining manufacturing fee was to be paid in one lump sum after the equipment was installed, debugged, and accepted at Yantai Metallurgical Institute. After the two contracts were signed, Yantai Metallurgical Institute paid Jilin Equipment Plant RMB 236,000 in processing fees.  

Due to factors such as increases in raw material prices, on December 2, 1988, the parties negotiated and signed the “Supplementary Agreement on the Contract for Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute Entrusting Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant to Process and Manufacture the Pre-Oxidation Furnace and Carbonization Furnace.” The supplementary agreement provided that the original cost of the pre-oxidation furnace would be increased from RMB 350,000 to RMB 650,000, and that of the asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace would be increased from RMB 420,000 to RMB 1,220,000. Within two weeks after the supplementary agreement took effect, Yantai Metallurgical Institute was to prepay Jilin Equipment Plant 50% of the newly added manufacturing cost of RMB 1,100,000, i.e., RMB 550,000. The remaining sum was to be paid in one lump sum after the equipment was installed, debugged, and accepted. The delivery dates for the two pieces of equipment were postponed to the end of March 1989 and the end of May 1989, respectively. If the equipment was delayed in delivery, Yantai Metallurgical Institute was to deduct RMB 2,000 for each day of delay from the unpaid amount. After Yantai Metallurgical Institute signed and sealed the supplementary agreement, when Jilin Equipment Plant took it back to Jilin for signing and sealing, Jilin Equipment Plant changed the content of Article 2 of the supplementary agreement from “the remaining sum shall be paid in one lump sum after the equipment is installed, debugged, and accepted” to “after the equipment arrives, 90% of the total payment shall be made, and the full amount shall be paid after installation, debugging, and acceptance,” changed the delivery deadlines to the end of April 1989 and the end of June 1989, changed Article 3(3) to provide that if the equipment was delayed in delivery and dispatch, Yantai Metallurgical Institute would deduct RMB 500 for each day of delay from the unpaid amount, and then signed and sealed the supplementary agreement and mailed it to Yantai Metallurgical Institute. After receiving the modified supplementary agreement, Yantai Metallurgical Institute raised no written objection.  

During the manufacturing and processing by Jilin Equipment Plant, due to the fact that some outsourced parts could not be delivered in a timely manner and other reasons, the final assembly of the equipment was affected. Therefore, the parties could not carry out the equipment handover according to the time stipulated in the contract. On May 5, 1989, October 10, 1989, and February 26, 1990, the parties negotiated the issues of delayed equipment delivery and payment. Yantai Metallurgical Institute acknowledged that the delivery date of the oxidation furnace was postponed to the end of June 1989, and the delivery date of the carbonization furnace was finally determined to be the end of April 1990. Jilin Equipment Plant ultimately delivered the equipment on August 5, 1989 for the oxidation furnace and June 20, 1990 for the carbonization furnace. On July 10, 1991, the parties signed the “Agreement on Debugging and Payment for the Oxidation Furnace and Carbonization Furnace.” The agreement provided that if quality problems were found during debugging, Jilin Equipment Plant would be responsible for handling them. After individual machine debugging had been carried out, remaining issues were to be dealt with in the next phase. Problems arising from manufacturing quality were to be resolved by Jilin Equipment Plant; problems arising from unreasonable design or processes were to be resolved with the assistance of Jilin Equipment Plant, which would not bear responsibility. Jilin Equipment Plant was to participate in the trial production of the pre-oxidation furnace and carbonization furnace. It was further agreed that after Yantai Metallurgical Institute paid RMB 20,000, Jilin Equipment Plant would send personnel to complete the debugging. The remaining amount was to be given priority for payment when funds became available that year, with the aim of settling by the end of the year. Article 6 of the agreement provided that this agreement had the same legal effect as the original contract and the supplementary agreement, and in case of conflict, this agreement would prevail. After Yantai Metallurgical Institute paid the RMB 20,000, Jilin Equipment Plant sent personnel to carry out debugging again, but no acceptance procedures were completed. The pre-oxidation furnace and the carbonization furnace were also not put into trial production. Yantai Metallurgical Institute made partial payments for the processing fees to Jilin Equipment Plant from time to time, but still owed RMB 525,835.56 in processing fees. On November 11, 1992, Yantai Metallurgical Institute, by letter (92) Yan Ye Cai Zi No. 7, acknowledged to Jilin Equipment Plant that it still owed more than RMB 530,000 in equipment fees. On March 31, 1994, when Yantai Metallurgical Institute and Jilin Equipment Plant reconciled their accounts, Yantai Metallurgical Institute stated: “Due to the current tight funds of our institute, the balance cannot be paid. When funds become available, our institute will pay the equipment fees.” When Jilin Equipment Plant demanded payment of the balance, Yantai Metallurgical Institute refused payment on the grounds of delayed delivery and unqualified equipment quality. A dispute arose, and the matter was brought to court.  

During the retrial of this Court, the parties were organized to inspect the equipment installation site. Yantai Metallurgical Institute pointed out that the problems with the pre-oxidation furnace were: the equipment sealing did not meet the design standards, the furnace bottom plate was cracked, and the rolling mesh belt of the oxidation furnace was off-track. The problems with the carbonization furnace were: the model of the differential pressure transmitter did not meet the design standards, etc. Jilin Equipment Plant denied these facts during the evidentiary hearing of this Court, arguing that the possibility of human damage to the equipment could not be ruled out, and requested that the equipment be appraised.  

The Jilin City Intermediate People’s Court, after trial, held that the processing and fabrication contract and the debugging and payment agreement of July 10, 1991, signed by Jilin Equipment Plant and Yantai Metallurgical Institute, were valid, and that Yantai Metallurgical Institute’s failure to pay as agreed constituted a breach of contract. The court ruled: Yantai Metallurgical Institute shall pay Jilin Equipment Plant the equipment processing fee of RMB 525,835.56; overdue payment liquidated damages of RMB 249,246.05; and bear the case acceptance fee of RMB 12,760.82.  

Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Yantai Metallurgical Institute appealed to the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court. After trial at second instance, the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court held that the facts found by the original trial were clear and the application of law was appropriate, and ruled: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 12,760.82 was to be borne by Yantai Metallurgical Institute.  

Dissatisfied with the final judgment of the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court, Yantai Metallurgical Institute applied to this Court for retrial. This Court referred the application to the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court for review. The Jilin Provincial High People’s Court conducted a retrial of the case. In the retrial, it held that the facts found in the first and second instances were not erroneous. Because the parties had cooperated well, no acceptance procedures were completed after the equipment debugging. The original trial did not recognize the “Supplementary Agreement on the Contract for Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute Entrusting Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant to Process and Manufacture the Pre-Oxidation Furnace and Carbonization Furnace” on the ground that, during the sealing process, Jilin Equipment Plant had unilaterally modified the agreement, which did not reflect the true intentions of both parties, and therefore it was invalid. However, since there was no dispute regarding the adjustment of the equipment price, this fact should be respected. The finding that there was no late delivery was improper. Pursuant to Article 153(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. Affirm Civil Judgment (1997) Ji Jing Zhong Zi No. 102; 2. Jilin Equipment Plant shall pay Yantai Metallurgical Institute liquidated damages for late delivery of RMB 28,785.  

Dissatisfied with the above retrial judgment, Yantai Metallurgical Institute applied to this Court for retrial, stating: The facts found in the original trial were unclear. After the processing and fabrication contract was signed, Jilin Equipment Plant signed a supplementary agreement with Yantai Metallurgical Institute, increasing the equipment processing fee by RMB 1,220,000. Jilin Equipment Plant not only delivered the equipment late but also failed to debug the delivered equipment to an acceptable standard. While paying the equipment fees, Yantai Metallurgical Institute repeatedly urged Jilin Equipment Plant to come for debugging. When Jilin Equipment Plant sent personnel several times to demand payment, the applicant refused payment and stated that personnel must be sent as soon as possible to debug the equipment, and payment would be made only after acceptance. As for the materials issued by the finance department, they were merely account reconciliation statements and could not prove that the equipment had been debugged and accepted. The original trial set the last debugging date as June 1991, while ignoring the fact that joint debugging took place from August to November 1991. This debugging resulted in a phase debugging summary recognized by all three parties — Yantai Metallurgical Institute, Jilin Equipment Plant, and the design unit. The summary clearly specified the existing problems with the equipment and how to resolve them. The problems not yet resolved during debugging were to be resolved by Jilin Equipment Plant. However, Jilin Equipment Plant never sent anyone for further debugging. The retrial’s finding that “the parties cooperated well and no acceptance procedures were completed” was inconsistent with the facts. Yantai Metallurgical Institute would not have agreed to exchange the price of qualified products for unqualified equipment. The applicant requested this Court to amend the judgment according to law. Jilin Equipment Plant, in its defense, argued that the facts found in the original trial were clear and the application of law was correct, that Jilin Equipment Plant had debugged the equipment to an acceptable standard, and that there was no issue of late delivery. The real reason for Yantai Metallurgical Institute’s failure to pay was its tight financial situation. The phase debugging summary of the pre-oxidation furnace and carbonization furnace submitted by Yantai Metallurgical Institute was false evidence, and Yantai Metallurgical Institute had lost the right to seek legal protection. Jilin Equipment Plant requested that the original judgment be upheld.  

In its retrial, this Court holds:  
The processing and fabrication contracts for the pre-oxidation furnace and the asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace signed by Yantai Metallurgical Institute and Jilin Equipment Plant, and the agreement on debugging and payment for the pre-oxidation furnace and carbonization furnace signed on July 10, 1991, were the true expressions of the parties’ intentions. The contents of the contracts did not violate legal provisions, and the original trial correctly found them valid. As for the supplementary agreement negotiated and signed by the parties on December 2, 1988, after Jilin Equipment Plant modified certain terms during the sealing process and mailed it back to Yantai Metallurgical Institute, Yantai Metallurgical Institute accepted the modified supplementary agreement and raised no written objection. Therefore, the supplementary agreement should also be deemed valid. The retrial judgment’s finding that the agreement was unilaterally modified by Jilin Equipment Plant during the sealing process and did not reflect the true intentions of both parties, hence was invalid, but that the adjustment of the equipment price was undisputed and should be upheld, effectively splits the supplementary agreement into two parts, deeming the first half valid and the second half invalid. This constitutes an improper finding of fact and shall be corrected.  

Yantai Metallurgical Institute argued that the equipment debugged by Jilin Equipment Plant was unqualified, that the parties had not completed any acceptance procedures to date, and submitted the phase debugging summary as evidence. Since the summary was not signed or sealed by Jilin Equipment Plant, and there was no other evidence proving that Jilin Equipment Plant had received the phase debugging summary, it cannot be used as evidence. According to the contract, the obligation to install and debug the two pieces of equipment fell on Jilin Equipment Plant. From this Court’s on-site inspection of the equipment, it is now impossible to determine, due to the prolonged storage of the equipment, whether the sealing of the pre-oxidation furnace meets the design standards and whether the rolling mesh belt is off-track. However, the problems of cracks in the bottom steel plate of the pre-oxidation furnace and the installation of a differential pressure transmitter for the carbonization furnace that does not match the model specified in the design drawings are objectively existing issues. Such quality problems do not involve whether the design is reasonable, because whether the design is reasonable and whether the manufactured equipment has production value are not Jilin Equipment Plant’s obligations. Jilin Equipment Plant’s obligation was to manufacture and install the equipment in accordance with the contract, debug it to an acceptable standard, and then deliver it to Yantai Metallurgical Institute. Although Jilin Equipment Plant conducted multiple debugging sessions, the parties did not complete any equipment acceptance procedures, nor was there any other evidence proving that the equipment had been debugged to an acceptable standard. Jilin Equipment Plant’s argument, based solely on the fact that Yantai Metallurgical Institute made partial payments for the equipment, that the equipment had been debugged to an acceptable standard lacks evidentiary force. Delivering qualified workpieces to the ordering party is the contractor’s obligation, while making timely payments to the contractor is the ordering party’s obligation. The rights they enjoy and the obligations they assume are different. Since Jilin Equipment Plant cannot provide evidence that the equipment was debugged to an acceptable standard, it shall be found that Jilin Equipment Plant delivered unqualified equipment to Yantai Metallurgical Institute. Because the two pieces of equipment have been stored for too long, the conditions for a new appraisal no longer exist. Therefore, this Court does not grant Jilin Equipment Plant’s request for a new appraisal. The retrial judgment’s finding, based on the parties’ good cooperation and the absence of acceptance procedures, that Jilin Equipment Plant had delivered qualified equipment constitutes an improper application of law and shall be corrected.  

The modified supplementary agreement of December 2, 1988, on the “Supplementary Agreement on the Contract for Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute Entrusting Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant to Process and Manufacture the Pre-Oxidation Furnace and Carbonization Furnace” provided that after the equipment arrived, 90% of the total payment would be made, and the full amount would be paid after installation, debugging, and acceptance. Jilin Equipment Plant delivered the equipment on August 5, 1989 for the oxidation furnace and June 20, 1990 for the carbonization furnace. On July 10, 1991, the parties signed the “Agreement on Debugging and Payment for the Oxidation Furnace and Carbonization Furnace,” which again changed the payment method. Jilin Equipment Plant did not object to Yantai Metallurgical Institute’s delayed payment. Therefore, Yantai Metallurgical Institute’s delayed payment may not be pursued. However, Yantai Metallurgical Institute only contacted Jilin Equipment Plant by telephone regarding the problems with the equipment debugging, without raising a written objection, and thus also bears fault. Yantai Metallurgical Institute acknowledged that it still owed part of the equipment processing fee; therefore, it shall bear corresponding civil liability for this part of the delayed payment.  

Jilin Equipment Plant delivered the pre-oxidation furnace 35 days late and the carbonization furnace 60 days late. According to the supplementary agreement, the equipment fee was to be deducted by RMB 500 per day of late delivery, and the parties should perform in accordance with the contract. The original trial’s award of liquidated damages of RMB 28,785 from Jilin Equipment Plant to Yantai Metallurgical Institute for late delivery lacks factual basis and shall be corrected.  

Article 29 of the Economic Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China provides: If a contract cannot be performed or cannot be fully performed due to the fault of one party, that party shall bear the liability for breach of contract; if both parties are at fault, each party shall bear its respective liability for breach of contract according to the actual circumstances. Article 35 provides that the contractor’s liability: If the work delivered fails to meet the quality or quantity standards stipulated in the contract, the contractor shall repair it free of charge, make up the shortfall, or reduce the remuneration; if the work product has major defects, the contractor shall also bear liability for compensation. The ordering party’s liability: If payment is made beyond the time limit stipulated in the contract, the ordering party shall pay liquidated damages for late payment. Article 13 of the Regulations on Processing and Fabrication Contracts provides: The contractor shall complete the work in accordance with the technical conditions specified in the contract and the ordering party’s requirements. Without the ordering party’s consent, the contractor shall not make any unauthorized changes. The contractor shall be responsible for the quality of all work undertaken. Article 21, paragraph 1 on the contractor’s liability for breach of contract provides: If the workpiece delivered or the work completed does not meet the quality standards stipulated in the contract, and the ordering party agrees to use it, the price shall be determined based on the quality; if the ordering party does not agree to use it, the contractor shall repair or replace it and bear liability for late delivery; if after repair or replacement it still does not meet the contract requirements, the ordering party has the right to reject it, and the resulting losses shall be compensated by the contractor. Paragraph 5 provides: If the contractor is unable to deliver the workpiece or complete the work, it shall pay liquidated damages of 10% to 30% of the total value of the part that cannot be delivered or completed, or 20% to 60% of the total remuneration. Article 22, paragraph 5 on the ordering party’s liability provides: If payment is made beyond the time limit stipulated in the contract, the ordering party shall pay liquidated damages to the contractor by reference to the People’s Bank of China’s provisions on late payment; if calculated on the basis of remuneration, for each day of delay, liquidated damages shall be paid at one-thousandth of the total remuneration.  

Accordingly, this Court, in accordance with the above laws and Article 153(1)(3) and Article 184(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, renders judgment as follows:  

1. Revoke Civil Judgment (1998) Ji Jing Zai Zi No. 26 and Civil Judgment (1997) Ji Jing Zhong Zi No. 102 of the Jilin Provincial High People’s Court, and Civil Judgment (1996) Ji Jing Chu Zi No. 80 of the Jilin City Intermediate People’s Court of Jilin Province;  

2. The pre-oxidation furnace and asphalt carbon fiber carbonization furnace processed by Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant shall be disposed of by Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute on its own;  

3. Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant shall pay Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute liquidated damages of RMB 673,200 for failure to deliver qualified equipment;  

4. Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant shall pay Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute liquidated damages of RMB 47,500 for late delivery of equipment;  

5. Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute shall pay Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant the outstanding equipment fee of RMB 525,835.56;  

6. Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute shall pay Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant liquidated damages of RMB 323,388.87 for late payment;  

7. Dismiss all other claims of both parties.

The aforementioned payment shall be made within ten days from the date of receipt of this judgment, and delayed payment shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fees for first and second instance are each RMB 12,760.82, totaling RMB 25,521.64, to be borne by Jilin Metallurgical Electromechanical Equipment Manufacturing Plant in the amount of RMB 15,312.98, and by Yantai Metallurgical New Materials Research Institute in the amount of RMB 10,208.66.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Gong Ming

Acting Judge: Sun Jigang

Acting Judge: Chen Jia

January 17, 2003

Clerk: Wang Yunfei

Profile of the Presiding Judge

Gong Ming, senior judge: born in 1962, Master of Laws. Since 2000, he has served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Trial Supervision Division of the Supreme People's Court.
